html:
The Mangarayi, also written Mangarrayi, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory, on the upper Roper River around present-day Mataranka. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.

Their neighbours were the Ngalakgan to the east, the Jawoyn to the northwest and the Yangman and Alawa to the south and southeast. The Elsey cattle station was set up on their land in the early 1880s. Jeannie Gunn, wife of its manager, wrote about life there in We of the Never Never (1908), one of the best known Australian books of its time, in which Mangarayi people appear, seen through settler eyes. Their language now has very few speakers.
